RankZeroOneBSD.title: Elliptic curves, Part II: rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory
RankZeroOneBSD.reason: Make Elliptic curves the first prerequisite and sole owner of its general foundations, including its still-planned Layer 7 targets. Preserve the member ID and all twelve stage IDs. The continuation owns quadratic analytic/arithmetic comparisons, the all-curve rank-zero/one rank and whole-Sha theorems, the separately proved source-qualified prime branches, all-prime certificates and rigorous tests; it does not assert the all-prime formula for every curve.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves.reason: Immutable upstream anchor. No title, scope, layer, implementation-status or consumer edits are proposed for it.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0.keeps: Adapters from the imported actual elliptic L-function to its finite central vanishing order, nonvanishing and derivative criteria, root-number parity, and quadratic-twist/base-change local-factor, product and central-derivative comparisons. Reuse generic analytic-order machinery. Transport the existing quadratic-twist object and rational-newform coefficient data; do not reconstruct the twist, modularity, curve/newform L-series equality or analytic continuation.
RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0.reason: The README already cites these suppliers. R29.3 owns rationality of the newform coefficient field; R29.6 owns the actual curve/newform analytic comparison. The quadratic base-change comparisons and actual analytic-rank interface remain new BSD work.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.1.keeps: Quadratic restriction/trace and twist comparisons on the existing point and torsion-quotient types; rational eigenspace/rank splitting; the specialized integral lattice index; odd-primary finite-level Selmer/Sha comparisons and explicit 2-primary kernels/cokernels; ramified-place differential, component and period comparisons; and descent of whole-Sha finiteness using a finite restriction kernel. Import general Mordell-Weil, height/regulator APIs, Selmer/Sha/Kummer carriers, local Tamagawa data, periods and Cassels invariance rather than rebuilding them.
RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.1.reason: A point equivalence or finite 2-descent API is not the required rank/index or general Selmer/Sha comparison. Preserve those missing comparison proofs, including the integral 2-primary corrections and the noncircular whole-Sha finiteness descent.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2.reason: Owns the source-qualified quadratic nonvanishing theorem with simultaneous local conditions, including the separate value and derivative branches and BFH/Friedberg-Hoffstein argument. This is not a consequence of the upstream twist construction or a root-number calculation.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.3.reason: Retain the all-E/Q analytic-rank-one theorem and entire-Sha finiteness, using GZ.8, HE.7 and BSD.1-2, including CM and nonsemistable cases and noncircular eigenspace descent. Neither Mordell-Weil nor finite Selmer groups proves this endpoint.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.4.reason: Retain the independent rank-zero twist/Heegner route, entire-Sha finiteness, the explicitly scoped Kato comparison and the combined analytic-rank-at-most-one interface. Do not make the universal endpoint depend on a restricted prime-part main conjecture.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5.keeps: Rationality and positivity of the actual normalized leading term in ranks zero and one; the specialized Heegner-point height/index comparison with torsion and Q/K factors; the Ribet-Takahashi character-group/parametrization-degree calculation; and a nonzero rational BSD defect with its valuation formula. Derive isogeny invariance of that rational defect by composing the imported arithmetic-quotient and actual analytic-leading-term invariances with the normalization adapters. Do not reprove Cassels, general isogeny Euler-factor/continuation invariance, the height/regulator and basis-independence API, or source-wide height/period rescaling.
RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5.reason: The immutable EllipticCurves Layer 7 stretch target owns both halves of general isogeny invariance. Its ownership is independent of implementation status. The rational BSD defect and specialized Heegner/modular-degree comparisons are additional outputs and cannot be deleted.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6.reason: Retain exactly the enumerated irreducible prime-part formulas, JSW and corrected Castella hypotheses, integral control maps and both divisibilities. No extension to every prime or every reduction type follows from this restructuring.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6a.reason: Retain sole ownership of the separately required signed/supersingular and corrected multiplicative proof inputs, including the BSTW replacement-source zeta-element argument and comparisons. Consume only early MIMC formulations/comparisons; export the completed branch to MIMC:L6, never import that reexport as a proof.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.7.reason: Retain the source-qualified good Eisenstein prime-part formulas, including the distinct CGS and Keller-Yin ranges and all rational p-torsion corrections. The irreducible main conjecture does not supply these branches.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.7a.reason: Retain sole ownership of the CGS/Keller-Yin arithmetic proof inputs with both divisibilities, integrality, local invariants, lattices and finite-submodule corrections. It uses early HE.8 classes, not HE.8b equality; its exports to HE.8b and MIMC:L6 are unchanged.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.8.reason: Retain the separate all-prime certificate: a positive rational defect, a proved finite exceptional support, every exceptional-prime equality and the outside-support statement. Rank/Sha finiteness and named prime-part results remain usable without this certificate. Existing arithmetic invariants are imported, not duplicated.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.9.keeps: Separate rank, whole-Sha finiteness, named-prime and complete-certificate APIs; rigorous enclosures for actual L-values/derivatives; and all existing positive and negative end-to-end tests, including torsion, rank-zero regulator one, normalization rescaling, CM, nonsemistable and p-isogeny cases. The regulator-one, torsion and general rescaling lemmas are imported inputs to these tests, not new foundation milestones.
RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.9.reason: Reusing a proved lemma does not justify deleting the acceptance test that checks its use in the BSD normalization. An unresolved exceptional prime must continue to block only the full leading-term certificate.
